identity: A first-person story with a real emotional arc (doubt -> discovery -> resolution) told over beautifully-shot mundane b-roll of the narrator's life. Typography works in TWO registers: tiny italic-serif 'whisper' words for connective narration, and large display words that land ONLY on emotional peaks. Slow by reel standards, warm-dark grade, phone-screen inserts when other content is discussed. The longest family in the corpus.

cinematic-story.notes: 'a video nearly made me quit' arc; kettle/lamp/couch b-roll; repeated display word ('failure' x3) at the low point; inset phone-UI clips for the video being discussed; ends on a direct 'you.'

rules.arc: beginning states the disruption ('today X happened'), middle descends (doubt visualized in dark frames and repeated negative display words), turn names the discovery (a person/idea, given a display-word introduction), end resolves with a direct-address line
rules.footage: static or slow-moving cinematic compositions of ordinary life (kitchen, desk, bed, mirror); the narrator appears but rarely faces camera; darkness and lamplight do the emotional work

typography.whisper: small italic serif, lowercase, placed in shadows/corners, for connective phrases
typography.peaks: large display words ONLY at emotional peaks; repetition of one word across consecutive frames marks the low point
typography.final: the last word addresses the viewer directly, alone on screen

rules.inserts: content being discussed appears as small inset clips/phone frames, never full-screen replacements
rules.pace: 2-3 cuts/10s; motion mean lowest in corpus (1.46) — stillness is the aesthetic

rubric.has_arc: disruption, descent, named turn, direct-address resolution — all four present

capability_notes: The register split maps to add_text sizes/fonts; insets are insert_media with fit/frames. The real dependency is TRANSCRIPT-DRIVEN PLANNING: the agent must find the arc (disruption/descent/turn/resolution) in the user's narration and place registers accordingly — a prompt-level planning grammar, not a new tool.
